1: """What an explanation artifact must say about the world that produced it.
   2: 
   3: An explanation is a *derived* artifact: every number in it was computed
   4: somewhere else, under conditions recorded somewhere else. So the header
   5: below carries two kinds of thing and nothing in between.
   6: 
   7: **A one-way reference to the source of record.** The Decision Card's
   8: manifest (HÄ-13) stays the single description of the run; an explanation
   9: points at it by path and checksum and copies **no field out of it**.
  10: Copying would create a second place where ``anchor_config_version`` is
  11: written down, and the two would eventually disagree â€” at which point the
  12: explanation would be describing a run that never happened while looking
  13: perfectly well-formed. :mod:`tests.test_explanation_contracts` asserts
  14: the header's field names do not intersect the manifest schema's, so this
  15: rule is enforced rather than remembered.
  16: 
  17: **Five versions the explanation layer owns.** These are the inputs the
  18: manifest cannot know about, and each one changes what the layer would
  19: output from byte-identical run data:
  20: 
  21: ``explanation_schema_version``
  22:     the shape of the ledger objects themselves.
  23: ``promotion_matrix_version``
  24:     the rules that turned records into claims. Two artifacts with the
  25:     same evidence and different matrix versions may legitimately carry
  26:     different claim levels; without this field that difference looks
  27:     like a bug in one of them.
  28: ``detector_version``
  29:     the detectors that produced the observations (E3).
  30: ``knowledge_base_version``
  31:     the curated KB entries a claim may cite (E3).
  32: ``tool_catalog_version``
  33:     which tool cards, at which versions, were on the menu.
  34: 
  35: Nothing here is optional and nothing has a default. A header that can
  36: omit a version is a header that will omit it exactly once, in the
  37: artifact somebody later needs to reproduce.
  38: """
  39: 
  40: from __future__ import annotations
  41: 
  42: import hashlib
  43: import re
  44: 
  45: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
  46: 
  47: from planbench_schemas.identity import canonical_json
  48: 
  49: #: Shape of the ledger objects in :mod:`planbench_explanation.ledger`.
  50: #: Bump MINOR to add an optional field, MAJOR to change or remove one.
  51: EXPLANATION_SCHEMA_VERSION = "0.1.0"
  52: 
  53: #: Version of the deterministic rules in
  54: #: :mod:`planbench_explanation.promotion`. Bump on **any** change that
  55: #: could move a claim between levels, including a change that only makes
  56: #: the layer stricter.
  57: PROMOTION_MATRIX_VERSION = "0.1.0"
  58: 
  59: #: Version of the checksum recipe below. Part of the payload, so an
  60: #: artifact hashed under an older recipe cannot silently compare equal to
  61: #: one hashed under a newer one.
  62: ARTIFACT_CHECKSUM_VERSION = "1"
  63: 
  64: #: Every checksum this layer stores is a SHA-256 hex digest, because
  65: #: every one of them is produced by the two functions above. Stating the
  66: #: shape lets a schema refuse ``"x"`` â€” a value that satisfies "not
  67: #: empty" and identifies nothing.
  68: CHECKSUM_PATTERN = r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
  69: 
  70: #: How a piece of running code is named: a full git commit, or a
  71: #: container digest. Both are what the manifest already records
  72: #: (``git_sha``, ``docker_image_digest``), so the explanation layer
  73: #: names code the same way rather than inventing a third convention.
  74: #:
  75: #: Short SHAs are refused on purpose. Seven hex characters identify a
  76: #: commit *in a repository at a moment*; the point of recording which
  77: #: build produced a checker result is that somebody can still resolve it
  78: #: after the repository has grown.
  79: CODE_REF_PATTERN = r"^(git:[0-9a-f]{40}|sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})$"
  80: 
  81: 
  82: def validate_code_ref(value: str, *, field: str) -> str:
  83:     """Check a git-commit or container-digest reference, or explain why not."""
  84:     if not re.fullmatch(CODE_REF_PATTERN, value):
  85:         raise ValueError(
  86:             f"{field}={value!r} is not a code reference; write git:<40 hex> for a "
  87:             "commit or sha256:<64 hex> for a container digest. A short SHA or a "
  88:             "free-form label cannot be resolved back to the build that ran."
  89:         )
  90:     return value
  91: 
  92: 
  93: class ExplanationArtifactHeader(BaseModel):
  94:     """Provenance every explanation artifact carries, before any content."""
  95: 
  96:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  97: 
  98:     #: Path of the manifest of the decision this explains, relative to the
  99:     #: artifact root. A reference, never a copy.
 100:     source_manifest_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 101:     #: SHA-256 of that manifest's bytes. The reference is worth nothing
 102:     #: without it: a manifest is a mutable file on disk, and an
 103:     #: explanation that outlived an edit of its source would keep
 104:     #: describing the run it was built from with no way to notice.
 105:     source_manifest_checksum: str = Field(pattern=CHECKSUM_PATTERN)
 106: 
 107:     explanation_schema_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 108:     promotion_matrix_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 109:     detector_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 110:     knowledge_base_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 111:     tool_catalog_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 112: 
 113:     @classmethod
 114:     def for_current_code(
 115:         cls,
 116:         *,
 117:         source_manifest_ref: str,
 118:         source_manifest_checksum: str,
 119:         detector_version: str,
 120:         knowledge_base_version: str,
 121:         tool_catalog_version: str,
 122:     ) -> ExplanationArtifactHeader:
 123:         """Header stamped with the versions this code implements.
 124: 
 125:         The two versions the *code* owns are filled in here rather than
 126:         by each caller, for the reason ``CONTRACTS_VERSION`` lives in one
 127:         module: a caller that passes its own idea of the schema version
 128:         will pass a stale one.
 129:         """
 130:         return cls(
 131:             source_manifest_ref=source_manifest_ref,
 132:             source_manifest_checksum=source_manifest_checksum,
 133:             explanation_schema_version=EXPLANATION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 134:             promotion_matrix_version=PROMOTION_MATRIX_VERSION,
 135:             detector_version=detector_version,
 136:             knowledge_base_version=knowledge_base_version,
 137:             tool_catalog_version=tool_catalog_version,
 138:         )
 139: 
 140: 
 141: def artifact_checksum(payload: object) -> str:
 142:     """SHA-256 of a JSON-safe payload, hashed the one canonical way.
 143: 
 144:     Reuses :func:`planbench_schemas.identity.canonical_json` so an
 145:     explanation artifact and a candidate id agree on what "the same
 146:     object" means. The recipe version is inside the hash, not beside it.
 147:     """
 148:     body = canonical_json({"v": ARTIFACT_CHECKSUM_VERSION, "payload": payload})
 149:     return hashlib.sha256(body.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
 150: 
 151: 
 152: def file_checksum(data: bytes) -> str:
 153:     """SHA-256 of raw file bytes â€” what ``source_manifest_checksum`` holds."""
 154:     return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

   2: 
   3: Everything upstream of here produces facts: the waterfall takes Î”U
   4: apart, the detectors say what happened, the lattice says what that rules
   5: out, the map says how wide the corridor was. The packet is where those
   6: arrive as one document, and it is deliberately the *whole* input: an
   7: analyst â€” human or model â€” never opens a Parquet file.
   8: 
   9: **Because reading the trace is where fabrication starts.** Give a model
  10: 546 rows of telemetry and it will produce a number that looks like a
  11: measurement and is not one. Give it a packet, and every number in its
  12: answer either appears here or is a number it invented, which is a
  13: difference a reviewer can check by looking.
  14: 
  15: **Known unknowns are mandatory and structured.** Not a paragraph asking
  16: the analyst to be careful â€” a list of claim types the orchestrator
  17: *refuses to promote*, each naming what makes it unavailable. A packet
  18: with an empty list would be claiming the platform knows everything about
  19: this run, and the H4 accounting gaps alone mean that is never true
  20: today, which is why :data:`STANDING_UNKNOWNS` exists rather than each
  21: caller remembering.
  22: 
  23: **Nothing in the packet is a claim.** Observations are patterns, the
  24: lattice reading is a constraint on attribution, the map features are

  70: class RobotFacts(BaseModel):
  71:     """The robot, as the two numbers a geometric argument needs."""
  72: 
  73:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)
  74: 
  75:     radius_m: float = Field(gt=0)
  76:     #: The costmap's inflation margin **beyond** the robot's own radius,
  77:     #: per side. Recorded so :attr:`required_passage_width_m` can be
  78:     #: checked against the parts it was derived from rather than taken
  79:     #: on trust.
  80:     inflation_margin_m: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
  81:     #: **The narrowest corridor this configuration can drive through**,
  82:     #: as a width: ``2 * (radius + inflation_margin)``. ``None`` when the
  83:     #: run did not record the inflation â€” absent rather than assumed,
  84:     #: because a clearance argument built on a guessed inflation is an
  85:     #: argument about a costmap nobody configured.
  86:     #:
  87:     #: It was called ``required_clearance_m`` and documented as "radius
  88:     #: plus the costmap's inflation", which is a **radius**, and it was
  89:     #: being compared against ``narrowest_passage_m``, which is a
  90:     #: **cross-section**. Both halves of a corridor have to clear, so the
  91:     #: comparison was short by a factor of two and a 0.50 m doorway read
  92:     #: as passable for a 0.26 m robot with a 0.22 m margin. Renamed so
  93:     #: the unit is in the name: two quantities that are not the same kind
  94:     #: of thing must not share a plausible name.
  95:     required_passage_width_m: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
  96: 
  97:     @property
  98:     def derived_passage_width_m(self) -> float | None:
  99:         """What the width should be, from the parts. ``None`` without a margin."""
 100:         if self.inflation_margin_m is None:
 101:             return None
 102:         return 2.0 * (self.radius_m + self.inflation_margin_m)

 132:     #: handed a 409. Those are precisely the runs somebody asks that
 133:     #: about. A Î”U decomposition is a statement about a *pair* the
 134:     #: statistics chose, and without a ranking there is no such pair â€”
 135:     #: but the sightings, the geometry and the gate table are all still
 136:     #: facts about this run, and they are what is left to look at.
 137:     waterfall: Waterfall | None = None
 138:     #: Gate verdicts as the report holds them: who was eliminated where.
 139:     gates: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
 140: 
 141: 
 142: class CasePacket(BaseModel):
 143:     """Everything an analyst may look at, and nothing else."""
 144: 
 145:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)
 146: 
 147:     header: ExplanationArtifactHeader
 148:     run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 149:     task: TaskFacts
 150:     #: Full stacks, not algorithm names. A candidate is a whole
 151:     #: navigation configuration (HÄ-1.1), and "RRT* is slow here" names
 152:     #: nothing that was measured.
 153:     candidates: tuple[CandidateComponents, ...]
 154:     decision: DecisionFacts
 155:     #: What the lattice rules out, per detection type. Mostly refusals,
 156:     #: and they are the most valuable part: they narrow what an analyst
 157:     #: may propose before it proposes anything.
 158:     lattice: tuple[ContrastFinding, ...] = ()
 159:     observations: tuple[Observation, ...] = ()
 160:     representative_episodes: ExemplarSet | None = None
 161:     known_unknowns: tuple[KnownUnknown, ...]
 162:     #: The fairness lane this evidence came from (Â§5.10). A research-lane
 163:     #: packet is diagnostic evidence and never a card statistic.
 164:     evidence_class: str = Field(min_length=1)
 165: 
 166:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 167:     def _check(self) -> CasePacket:
 168:         if not self.known_unknowns:
 169:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 170:                 "a packet with no known unknowns claims the platform knows everything "
 171:                 "about this run; the H4 accounting gaps alone make that untrue today. "
 172:                 "Start from STANDING_UNKNOWNS"
 173:             )
 174:         if len(self.candidates) < 2:
 175:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 176:                 "a packet explains a comparison, and a comparison needs two candidates"
 177:             )
 178:         known = {item.candidate_id for item in self.candidates}
 179:         waterfall = self.decision.waterfall
 180:         if waterfall is not None:
 181:             compared = {waterfall.candidate_a, waterfall.candidate_b}
 182:             if not compared <= known:
 183:                 raise CasePacketRefusal(
 184:                     f"the waterfall compares {sorted(compared)} but the packet describes "
 185:                     f"{sorted(known)}; an analyst reading this would be explaining a "
 186:                     "comparison between candidates it cannot see"
 187:                 )
 188:         strangers = {item.candidate_id for item in self.observations} - known
 189:         if strangers:
 190:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 191:                 f"observations name candidate(s) {sorted(strangers)} that are not in this packet"
 192:             )
 193:         lattice_strangers = {
 194:             candidate_id
 195:             for finding in self.lattice
 196:             for pair in finding.pairs
 197:             for candidate_id in pair
 198:         } - known
 199:         if lattice_strangers:
 200:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 201:                 f"the lattice reading rests on candidate(s) {sorted(lattice_strangers)} "
 202:                 "that are not in this packet; a contrast from another run would read as "
 203:                 "a constraint on this one"
 204:             )
 205: 
 206:         if self.representative_episodes is not None and waterfall is None:
 207:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 208:                 "this packet carries exemplars and no waterfall. Three of the four "
 209:                 "roles are defined against the pair Î”U was computed for, so exemplars "
 210:                 "without a ranking are four episodes with labels nothing earned"
 211:             )
 212:         if self.representative_episodes is not None and waterfall is not None:
 213:             # **Ordered**, not a set. ``strongest_for_winner`` is defined
 214:             # against whichever candidate Î”U was computed *for*, so an
 215:             # exemplar set built the other way round is the same four
 216:             # episodes with two of the labels swapped.
 217:             ordered = (
 218:                 self.representative_episodes.candidate_a,
 219:                 self.representative_episodes.candidate_b,
 220:             )
 221:             expected = (waterfall.candidate_a, waterfall.candidate_b)
 222:             if ordered != expected:
 223:                 raise CasePacketRefusal(
 224:                     f"the exemplars are about {ordered} and the waterfall about "
 225:                     f"{expected}; the same pair the other way round relabels "
 226:                     "'best for the winner' as the runner-up's best episode"
 227:                 )
 228:         return self
 229: 
 230:     @property
 231:     def blocked_claim_types(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 232:         """Every claim type this packet forbids, deduplicated and sorted.
 233: 
 234:         Convenience for a caller wiring the promotion matrix, so the
 235:         enforcement reads from the packet rather than from a list
 236:         somebody kept in step by hand.
 237:         """
 238:         return tuple(
 239:             sorted({kind for unknown in self.known_unknowns for kind in unknown.blocks_claim_types})
 240:         )
 241: 
 242: 
 243: def build_case_packet(
 244:     *,
 245:     run_id: str,
 246:     header: ExplanationArtifactHeader,
 247:     task: TaskFacts,
 248:     candidates: Sequence[CandidateComponents],
 249:     decision: DecisionFacts,
 250:     lattice: Sequence[ContrastFinding] = (),
 251:     observations: Sequence[Observation] = (),
 252:     representative_episodes: ExemplarSet | None = None,
 253:     extra_unknowns: Sequence[KnownUnknown] = (),
 254:     evidence_class: str = "production",
 255: ) -> CasePacket:
 256:     """Assemble one packet from parts every other module already made.
 257: 
 258:     **A packet with no comparison is still a packet.** See
 259:     :attr:`DecisionFacts.waterfall`: a run that ranked nobody has
 260:     sightings, geometry and a gate table, and those are the evidence
 261:     somebody asking "why did it fail" needs. What it does not have is a
 262:     pair, so it carries no waterfall and no exemplars â€” and the panel
 263:     matrix already knows not to draw either.
 264: 
 265:     A composition, on purpose. Detectors, the waterfall, the lattice and
 266:     the exemplar recipe are each testable alone and each refuse their
 267:     own bad inputs; a builder that recomputed any of them here would be
 268:     a second implementation to keep in step.
 269: 
 270:     ``extra_unknowns`` are added to :data:`STANDING_UNKNOWNS` rather than
 271:     replacing them: a caller who knows about one more gap should not be
 272:     able to drop the ones that always apply.
 273:     """
 274:     unknowns = list(STANDING_UNKNOWNS)
 275:     seen = {unknown.id for unknown in unknowns}
 276:     for unknown in extra_unknowns:
 277:         if unknown.id in seen:
 278:             raise CasePacketRefusal(
 279:                 f"known unknown {unknown.id!r} is already one of the standing gaps; "
 280:                 "two entries with one id would let a reader think two things were "
 281:                 "unavailable when one is"
 282:             )
 283:         seen.add(unknown.id)
 284:         unknowns.append(unknown)
 285: 
 286:     if header.knowledge_base_version != KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VERSION:
 287:         raise CasePacketRefusal(
 288:             f"header names knowledge base {header.knowledge_base_version!r} but this "
 289:             f"build carries {KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VERSION!r}; a packet whose citations "
 290:             "resolve against a different base is a packet nobody can re-read"
 291:         )
 292: 
 293:     return CasePacket(
 294:         header=header,
 295:         run_id=run_id,
 296:         task=task,
 297:         candidates=tuple(candidates),
 298:         decision=decision,
 299:         lattice=tuple(lattice),
 300:         observations=tuple(observations),
 301:         representative_episodes=representative_episodes,
 302:         known_unknowns=tuple(unknowns),
 303:         evidence_class=evidence_class,
 304:     )

1: """The evidence ladder a claim is placed on, and the words it may use.
   2: 
   3: Four levels, and *no fifth level for ignorance*. "Not enough evidence"
   4: is the absence of a claim, not a weak one â€” a fifth rung would let an
   5: empty investigation render as a row on the panel, which is how a reader
   6: learns to read blank space as a finding.
   7: 
   8: +--------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
   9: | level                    | what had to be true                       |
  10: +==========================+===========================================+
  11: | ``observed``             | it was measured, from recorded data       |
  12: | ``associated``           | a pattern is consistent with a mechanism  |
  13: | ``mechanism_verified``   | a checker reproduced the narrow condition |
  14: | ``intervention_supported``| the world was changed and the effect moved|
  15: +--------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
  16: 
  17: The level is a property of the **evidence**, never of the pipeline that
  18: produced the sentence. An LLM-written sentence and a template-written
  19: sentence backed by the same record sit on the same rung.
  20: 
  21: **Qualifiers are orthogonal.** They say where a number came from, and
  22: they never move a claim up or down: ``profile_weighted`` (the
  23: decomposition depends on the preference profile, so the profile must be
  24: named or a preference is being read as a measurement), ``estimated`` (a
  25: tool's estimate, not a raw measurement), ``reconstructed_input`` (inputs
  26: were rebuilt and not verified) and ``research_lane`` (evidence from a
  27: diagnostic run outside the evaluation distribution).
  28: 
  29: **Why a phrase whitelist exists at all.** The failure this blocks is not
  30: a fabricated number â€” the ledger already stops those. It is
  31: ``"stuck *because of* a local minimum [fact:oscillation_B7]"``: real
  32: citation, real observation, invented causality. That is a *lexical*
  33: defect and can be caught lexically, so it is, at render time (E4) and in
  34: review, using the same table the promotion matrix uses.
  35: 
  36: The phrases below are English because the platform's exported report is
  37: English. A locale is a :class:`PhrasePolicy`, not a fork of this module:
  38: E4 adds one for the Vietnamese UI and the rules stay in one place.
  39: """
  40: 
  41: from __future__ import annotations
  42: 
  43: import re
  44: from collections.abc import Iterable
  45: from typing import Literal
  46: 
  47: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
  48: 
  49: ClaimLevel = Literal["observed", "associated", "mechanism_verified", "intervention_supported"]
  50: 
  51: #: Weakest to strongest. Index in this tuple is the only ordering.
  52: CLAIM_LEVEL_ORDER: tuple[ClaimLevel, ...] = (
  53:     "observed",
  54:     "associated",
  55:     "mechanism_verified",
  56:     "intervention_supported",
  57: )
  58: 
  59: Qualifier = Literal[
  60:     "profile_weighted",
  61:     "estimated",
  62:     "reconstructed_input",
  63:     "research_lane",
  64: ]
  65: 
  66: KNOWN_QUALIFIERS: tuple[Qualifier, ...] = (
  67:     "profile_weighted",
  68:     "estimated",
  69:     "reconstructed_input",
  70:     "research_lane",
  71: )
  72: 
  73: 
  74: class UnknownClaimLevelError(ValueError):
  75:     """A level outside :data:`CLAIM_LEVEL_ORDER`."""
  76: 
  77: 
  78: def level_rank(level: ClaimLevel) -> int:
  79:     """Position on the ladder; higher is a stronger statement."""
  80:     try:
  81:         return CLAIM_LEVEL_ORDER.index(level)
  82:     except ValueError as exc:
  83:         raise UnknownClaimLevelError(
  84:             f"{level!r} is not a claim level; known levels are {list(CLAIM_LEVEL_ORDER)}"
  85:         ) from exc
  86: 
  87: 
  88: def weakest(*levels: ClaimLevel) -> ClaimLevel:
  89:     """The least of the given levels â€” every ceiling composes this way.
  90: 
  91:     A tool card's maximum, an input provenance ceiling and a subject
  92:     ceiling are three independent caps, and a claim may not exceed any
  93:     of them. Taking the minimum here rather than at each call site is
  94:     what stops one of the three being forgotten in one branch.
  95:     """
  96:     if not levels:
  97:         raise ValueError("weakest() needs at least one level")
  98:     return min(levels, key=level_rank)
  99: 
 100: 
 101: class PhrasePolicy(BaseModel):
 102:     """Which wordings each level may use, in one language."""
 103: 
 104:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 105: 
 106:     locale: str
 107:     #: Phrases permitted *at* a level. A phrase belonging to a stronger
 108:     #: level is forbidden at every weaker one â€” that is derived below,
 109:     #: not listed, so the two halves cannot drift apart.
 110:     allowed: dict[ClaimLevel, tuple[str, ...]]
 111:     #: Wordings forbidden everywhere below ``intervention_supported``
 112:     #: regardless of the table â€” the causal vocabulary readers weigh
 113:     #: most heavily.
 114:     causal: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 115: 
 116:     def forbidden_at(self, level: ClaimLevel) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 117:         """Phrases that may not appear in a sentence carrying ``level``."""
 118:         rank = level_rank(level)
 119:         stronger = {
 120:             phrase
 121:             for other, phrases in self.allowed.items()
 122:             if level_rank(other) > rank
 123:             for phrase in phrases
 124:         }
 125:         if rank < level_rank("intervention_supported"):
 126:             stronger.update(self.causal)
 127:         return tuple(sorted(stronger))
 128: 
 129:     def violations(self, text: str, level: ClaimLevel) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 130:         """Forbidden phrases present in ``text``, as written.
 131: 
 132:         Word-boundary matching, case-insensitive: ``"caused"`` must not
 133:         fire on ``"because"`` and must fire on ``"Caused"``.
 134:         """
 135:         lowered = text.lower()
 136:         return tuple(
 137:             phrase
 138:             for phrase in self.forbidden_at(level)
 139:             if re.search(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(phrase.lower())}(?!\w)", lowered)
 140:         )
 141: 
 142: 
 143: #: The English policy, matching the level table in the design note.
 144: ENGLISH_PHRASES = PhrasePolicy(
 145:     locale="en",
 146:     allowed={
 147:         "observed": ("measured", "recorded", "observed"),
 148:         "associated": ("consistent with", "matches the pattern of", "co-occurs with"),
 149:         "mechanism_verified": ("verified", "reproduced", "confirmed by replay"),
 150:         "intervention_supported": ("caused", "is the primary cause", "eliminates"),
 151:     },
 152:     causal=("because of", "due to", "causes", "caused by", "responsible for"),
 153: )
 154: 
 155: 
 156: def check_phrases(
 157:     text: str,
 158:     level: ClaimLevel,
 159:     *,
 160:     policy: PhrasePolicy = ENGLISH_PHRASES,
 161: ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 162:     """Convenience wrapper over :meth:`PhrasePolicy.violations`."""
 163:     return policy.violations(text, level)
 164: 
 165: 
 166: def canonical_qualifiers(values: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[Qualifier, ...]:
 167:     """Validate, deduplicate and sort qualifiers.
 168: 
 169:     Closed vocabulary for the same reason the observation tokens are
 170:     closed (``planbench_schemas.observations``): a qualifier compared by
 171:     string is a qualifier a typo turns off.
 172:     """
 173:     cleaned = {value.strip() for value in values}
 174:     unknown = sorted(cleaned - set(KNOWN_QUALIFIERS))
 175:     if unknown:
 176:         raise ValueError(
 177:             f"unknown qualifier(s) {unknown}; known qualifiers are {list(KNOWN_QUALIFIERS)}"
 178:         )
 179:     return tuple(sorted(cleaned))  # type: ignore[arg-type]

1: """The five ledger objects, and the powers each one deliberately lacks.
   2: 
   3: The explanation layer's central risk is not a wrong sentence â€” it is a
   4: sentence that *sounds* better supported than the data behind it. The
   5: defence is ownership, expressed in schemas rather than in validation
   6: rules applied after the fact:
   7: 
   8: ``HypothesisProposal``
   9:     everything an analyst â€” human or model â€” is allowed to return.
  10:     There is **no** status, confidence, level, or impact number in it.
  11:     Not "rejected if present": absent from the schema, so a proposal
  12:     carrying one fails to parse. Leaving a ``{delta, method}`` field in
  13:     the analyst's object and validating the number afterwards still
  14:     lets a model invent a number of exactly the right shape, and a
  15:     reviewer reading the artifact cannot tell invented from computed.
  16: ``CheckerResult``
  17:     what a tool host produced. Only the host writes these, and each one
  18:     carries a resolvable implementation reference and an evidence
  19:     checksum, so a result can be traced back to the build that made it.
  20: ``ImpactRef``
  21:     a pointer to a tool-produced artifact, plus the **kind** of impact
  22:     it describes. The two kinds are not interchangeable and the
  23:     distinction is the difference between an honest sentence and a
  24:     causal one â€” see :class:`ImpactRef`.
  25: ``InvestigationRecord``
  26:     the orchestrator's view: which proposal, adjudicated how, with
  27:     which results attached.
  28: ``Claim``
  29:     what the UI may render. Produced only by the deterministic
  30:     promotion matrix (:mod:`planbench_explanation.promotion`), never
  31:     written by hand and never by an analyst.
  32: 
  33: ``KnownUnknown`` sits alongside them. It is structured, not prose,
  34: because the orchestrator *enforces* it: a gap that blocks a claim type
  35: blocks it in code, rather than being a paragraph the analyst is trusted
  36: to have read.
  37: """
  38: 
  39: from __future__ import annotations
  40: 
  41: from typing import Any, Literal
  42: 
  43: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
  44: 
  45: from planbench_explanation.levels import ClaimLevel, Qualifier, canonical_qualifiers
  46: from planbench_explanation.propositions import (
  47:     PropositionType,
  48:     canonical_propositions,
  49:     require_assertable,
  50: )
  51: from planbench_explanation.provenance import (
  52:     ExecutionStatus,
  53:     InputProvenance,
  54:     PropositionVerdict,
  55: )
  56: from planbench_explanation.subjects import Subject
  57: from planbench_explanation.versioning import CHECKSUM_PATTERN, validate_code_ref
  58: 
  59: #: What an evidence reference points at.
  60: #:
  61: #: ``knowledge_entry`` is the one with a shape rule: a KB citation must
  62: #: pin an entry version (``kb:inflation_gap_closure@2``). An unversioned
  63: #: citation would let a curated entry be edited under a claim that was
  64: #: promoted before the edit.
  65: EvidenceKind = Literal[
  66:     "fact",
  67:     "observation",
  68:     "trace_window",
  69:     "artifact",
  70:     "knowledge_entry",
  71:     "plan_attempt",
  72:     "contrast",
  73: ]
  74: 
  75: 
  76: class EvidenceRef(BaseModel):
  77:     """One pointer into data the platform holds."""
  78: 
  79:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  80: 
  81:     ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
  82:     kind: EvidenceKind
  83:     provenance: InputProvenance = "recorded"
  84:     checksum: str | None = None
  85: 
  86:     @model_validator(mode="after")
  87:     def _check(self) -> EvidenceRef:
  88:         if self.kind == "knowledge_entry" and "@" not in self.ref:
  89:             raise ValueError(
  90:                 f"knowledge entry reference {self.ref!r} does not pin a version; "
  91:                 "write kb:<entry_id>@<entry_version> so an edit to the entry "
  92:                 "cannot silently change what an already-promoted claim cited"
  93:             )
  94:         if self.provenance == "missing" and self.checksum is not None:
  95:             raise ValueError("evidence that is missing cannot carry a checksum")
  96:         return self
  97: 
  98: 
  99: class KnownUnknown(BaseModel):
 100:     """A gap in the data, and the claim types it forbids."""
 101: 
 102:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 103: 
 104:     id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 105:     blocks_claim_types: tuple[PropositionType, ...]
 106:     source: str = Field(min_length=1)
 107: 
 108:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 109:     def _check(self) -> KnownUnknown:
 110:         if not self.blocks_claim_types:
 111:             raise ValueError(
 112:                 f"known unknown {self.id!r} blocks nothing; a gap that blocks no "
 113:                 "claim type is a note, and notes do not belong in the packet's "
 114:                 "enforced section"
 115:             )
 116:         canonical_propositions(self.blocks_claim_types, field="blocks_claim_types")
 117:         return self

 120: class RequestedCheck(BaseModel):
 121:     """A tool the analyst asks the host to run. A request, not a result."""
 122: 
 123:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 124: 
 125:     tool_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 126:     tool_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 127:     arguments: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

 130: class HypothesisProposal(BaseModel):
 131:     """Everything the analyst may return, and nothing else.
 132: 
 133:     ``extra="forbid"`` is load-bearing here, not hygiene: it is what
 134:     turns "the analyst must not report a confidence" from a policy into
 135:     a parse error.
 136:     """
 137: 
 138:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 139: 
 140:     hypothesis_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 141:     hypothesis_statement: str = Field(min_length=1)
 142:     proposition_type: PropositionType
 143:     proposed_subject: Subject
 144:     supports: tuple[EvidenceRef, ...] = ()
 145:     contradicts: tuple[EvidenceRef, ...] = ()
 146:     #: Evidence the analyst says is needed and absent. Structured
 147:     #: incompleteness beats a confident story built around a hole.
 148:     missing_evidence: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 149:     requested_checks: tuple[RequestedCheck, ...] = ()
 150:     #: Prose only, and always routed to the research lane for human
 151:     #: approval. No tool executes an experiment.
 152:     recommended_experiments: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 153: 
 154:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 155:     def _check(self) -> HypothesisProposal:
 156:         require_assertable(self.proposition_type, field="proposition_type")
 157:         return self

 160: class PropositionOutcome(BaseModel):
 161:     """One proposition a tool result speaks to."""
 162: 
 163:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 164: 
 165:     proposition_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 166:     proposition_type: PropositionType
 167:     result: PropositionVerdict

 170: class CheckerResult(BaseModel):
 171:     """A tool host's answer â€” the ledger's copy of a ToolResult.
 172: 
 173:     Three rules the schema enforces, each from a way the single word
 174:     ``pass`` used to hide a distinction:
 175: 
 176:     1. ``execution_status`` says how the run went; ``proposition_verdict``
 177:        says whether the proposition stood. A completed run that refutes
 178:        the hypothesis is a success and a dead claim.
 179:     2. A top-level ``proposition_verdict`` is only meaningful for a tool
 180:        speaking to exactly one proposition. Multi-proposition results
 181:        omit it and carry a verdict per entry.
 182:     3. A run that did not complete carries no verdict at all. Otherwise
 183:        ``not_checkable`` acquires an opinion it has no basis for.
 184: 
 185:     And one rule about traceability. A completed result must carry all
 186:     three of ``evidence_artifact_ref``, ``evidence_checksum`` and
 187:     ``implementation_ref``, and the last two must be **well formed** â€”
 188:     a 64-hex digest and a resolvable code reference (``git:<40 hex>`` or
 189:     ``sha256:<64 hex>``). They were optional in the first cut, and then
 190:     briefly required-but-unvalidated, which let ``"x"`` satisfy the
 191:     rule; a checksum that hashes nothing traces no better than a blank.
 192:     Non-completed results may omit them â€” a run that did not happen
 193:     produced no evidence to reference.
 194: 
 195:     **What this does and does not prove.** The schema makes a result
 196:     *traceable*: every field an auditor needs to go and look is present
 197:     and resolvable. It does **not** prove the tool host wrote it â€”
 198:     nothing verifies a signature here, and a caller with a plausible
 199:     digest can construct one. Authorship is enforced upstream, by the
 200:     host being the only writer of results into the ledger (E5/E6). Both
 201:     halves are needed and neither substitutes for the other, so neither
 202:     is described as if it were the other.
 203:     """
 204: 
 205:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 206: 
 207:     request_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 208:     tool_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 209:     tool_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 210:     execution_status: ExecutionStatus
 211:     input_provenance: InputProvenance
 212:     proposition_verdict: PropositionVerdict | None = None
 213:     supported_propositions: tuple[PropositionOutcome, ...] = ()

1: # PlanBench API.
   2: #
   3: # The repository is not pip-installable yet (no per-package pyproject),
   4: # so the image mirrors the layout and sets PYTHONPATH the same way the
   5: # local commands do. When the packages become installable this collapses
   6: # into a plain `pip install .` â€” until then, one convention, used
   7: # everywhere, beats two that can disagree.
   8: 
   9: FROM python:3.12-slim AS base
  10: 
  11: ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  12:     PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  13:     PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1
  14: 
  15: WORKDIR /app
  16: 
  17: # Dependencies first: they change far less often than the source, so
  18: # this layer stays cached across ordinary code edits.
  19: COPY docker/requirements-api.txt /tmp/requirements-api.txt
  20: RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/requirements-api.txt
  21: 
  22: COPY packages/ /app/packages/
  23: COPY services/ /app/services/
  24: COPY apps/api/ /app/apps/api/
  25: COPY alembic/ /app/alembic/
  26: COPY alembic.ini /app/alembic.ini
  27: COPY docs/ /app/docs/
  28: 
  29: ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/packages/schemas:/app/packages/planning:/app/packages/metrics:/app/packages/benchmark:/app/services/simulator:/app/services/tracking:/app/services/agent_service:/app/apps/api
  30: 
  31: # Artifacts are written here; compose mounts a volume so they survive a
  32: # container rebuild (they are referenced by URI from the database).
  33: ENV PLANBENCH_ARTIFACT_DIR=/data/artifacts
  34: RUN mkdir -p /data/artifacts
  35: 
  36: # Never run as root: a container that writes to a mounted volume as root
  37: # leaves files the host user cannot clean up.
  38: RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 planbench \
  39:     && chown -R planbench:planbench /data
  40: USER planbench
  41: 
  42: EXPOSE 8000
  43: 
  44: HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=5 \
  45:     CMD python -c "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/health', timeout=3).status == 200 else 1)"
  46: 
  47: CMD ["uvicorn", "planbench_api.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

1: # Ruff configuration â€” the single source of truth for this repository.
   2: #
   3: # A `ruff.toml` at the root **replaces** `[tool.ruff]` in pyproject.toml
   4: # rather than merging with it. When both existed, pyproject's settings
   5: # were silently ignored â€” including `known-first-party`, which is why CI
   6: # reported 36 import-sorting errors that never appeared locally. The
   7: # project's settings therefore live here, and pyproject.toml no longer
   8: # configures ruff at all.
   9: 
  10: # Matches `requires-python = ">=3.12"` in pyproject.toml. Linting against
  11: # an older target would accept syntax the project does not claim to run.
  12: target-version = "py312"
  13: line-length = 100
  14: 
  15: # `docs/` holds prose, including the T-011 programme's guide. Ruff would
  16: # reformat the Python snippets inside those Markdown files, which changes
  17: # what the guide teaches â€” not something a linter should decide.
  18: exclude = ["docs/"]
  19: 
  20: [lint]
  21: select = [
  22:     "E",   # pycodestyle errors
  23:     "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
  24:     "F",   # pyflakes
  25:     "I",   # isort
  26:     "N",   # pep8-naming
  27:     "B",   # flake8-bugbear
  28:     "UP",  # pyupgrade
  29:     "SIM", # flake8-simplify
  30:     "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
  31: ]
  32: 
  33: ignore = [
  34:     # N818 wants every exception class to end in `Error`. This codebase
  35:     # names them after the condition instead (`PermissionDenied`,
  36:     # `ModelNotAllowed`, `DatabaseUnavailable`), and those names are used
  37:     # across the API layer, the tests and the docs. Renaming twelve
  38:     # classes to satisfy a naming convention would be a wide, risky
  39:     # change for no behavioural gain.
  40:     "N818",
  41: ]
  42: 
  43: [lint.isort]
  44: # Without this the `planbench_*` packages sort as third-party, which is
  45: # exactly what broke CI: every test file's import block was reported
  46: # unsorted.
  47: known-first-party = [
  48:     "planbench_schemas",
  49:     "planbench_simulator",
  50:     "planbench_planning",
  51:     "planbench_metrics",
  52:     "planbench_benchmark",
  53:     "planbench_decision",
  54:     "planbench_explanation",
  55:     "planbench_tracking",
  56:     "planbench_rl",
  57:     "planbench_agent",
  58:     "planbench_api",
  59: ]
  60: 
  61: [format]
  62: quote-style = "double"
  63: indent-style = "space"

1: [project]
   2: name = "planbench"
   3: version = "0.1.0"
   4: description = "Agentic AI PlanBench â€” simulator and path/motion planning benchmark for AMR/AGV mobile robots (simulation only)."
   5: requires-python = ">=3.12"
   6: 
   7: # NOTE (Phase 1A): this repository is not yet packaged for installation.
   8: # Tests import the packages directly from source via the pytest
   9: # `pythonpath` setting below. Per-package pyproject files will be added
  10: # when other services need to install them (Phase 2+).
  11: 
  12: [tool.pytest.ini_options]
  13: testpaths = ["tests"]
  14: pythonpath = [
  15:     # The repository root, so `src.*` (the T-011 scaffold) resolves, and
  16:     # `tests/`, so shared helpers like `agent_fakes` import as top-level
  17:     # modules. Both used to work by accident: pytest puts a test file's
  18:     # first non-package parent on sys.path, and `tests/` had no
  19:     # `__init__.py`. Adding one turned `tests/` into a package and broke
  20:     # every `import agent_fakes`. Naming the paths here makes it work
  21:     # either way.
  22:     ".",
  23:     "tests",
  24:     "packages/schemas",
  25:     "packages/planning",
  26:     "packages/metrics",
  27:     "packages/benchmark",
  28:     "packages/decision",
  29:     "packages/explanation",
  30:     "packages/plugin_sdk",
  31:     "services/simulator",
  32:     "services/tracking",
  33:     "services/agent_service",
  34:     "ml",
  35:     "apps/api",
  36: ]
  37: 
  38: # Ruff is configured in `ruff.toml` at the repository root, not here.
  39: # A root `ruff.toml` replaces `[tool.ruff]` outright instead of merging
  40: # with it, so keeping settings in both places means one copy is silently
  41: # dead â€” which is how CI ended up disagreeing with local runs about
  42: # import order. One file, one answer.
  43: 
  44: [tool.coverage.run]
  45: branch = true

 217: # Always before the API starts. An API serving a schema older than its
 218: # code fails one request at a time, in ways that look like bugs; a
 219: # migration that fails here says so once, plainly, and stops.
 220: run_migrations() {
 221:   if [[ -z "$PLANBENCH_DATABASE_URL" ]]; then
 222:     # Reached when .env contains a bare `PLANBENCH_DATABASE_URL=`. That
 223:     # sets the variable to an empty string, so the default a few lines
 224:     # above never applies â€” a difference between "unset" and "set to
 225:     # nothing" that is easy to miss and costs a whole session's work.
 226:     warn "database  in-memory: maps, benchmarks and accounts are lost on restart."
 227:     warn "          PLANBENCH_DATABASE_URL is set to an empty string in .env."
 228:     warn "          To keep your data, put this in .env instead:"
 229:     warn "              PLANBENCH_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///$ROOT/planbench.db"
 230:     warn "          then run:  .venv/bin/alembic upgrade head"
 231:     return 0
 232:   fi
 233: 
 234:   if [[ ! -x "$ROOT/.venv/bin/alembic" ]]; then
 235:     die "alembic is missing from the virtualenv. Install it once:
 236:   '$ROOT/.venv/bin/pip' install alembic"
 237:   fi
 238: 
 239:   info "database  $PLANBENCH_DATABASE_URL"
 240: 
 241:   local output
 242:   if ! output="$(cd "$ROOT" && PYTHONPATH="$PY_PATH" \
 243:       "$ROOT/.venv/bin/alembic" upgrade head 2>&1)"; then
 244:     printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2

 246: Fix the error above, then run ./scripts/dev_stack.sh start again."
 247:   fi

 249:   info "migrations up to date"

 298: free_port() {
 299:   local port="$1"
 300:   local pids
 301:   local pid
 302: 
 303:   pids="$(
 304:     lsof -tiTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null ||
 305:       true
 306:   )"
 307: 
 308:   if [[ -z "$pids" ]]; then
 309:     return 0
 310:   fi
 311: 
 312:   info "port $port was in use â€” stopping pid(s) $(echo "$pids" | tr '\n' ' ')"
 313: 
 314:   # shellcheck disable=SC2086
 315:   kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true
 316: 
 317:   # Wait up to five seconds for the processes to stop.
 318:   for _ in {1..20}; do
 319:     pids="$(
 320:       lsof -tiTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null ||
 321:         true
 322:     )"
 323: 
 324:     if [[ -z "$pids" ]]; then
 325:       return 0
 326:     fi
 327: 
 328:     sleep 0.25
 329:   done
 330: 
 331:   warn "port $port is still in use; forcing the remaining process(es) to stop"
 332: 
 333:   # shellcheck disable=SC2086
 334:   kill -9 $pids 2>/dev/null || true
 335: }

 341: wait_for() {
 342:   local url="$1"
 343:   local label="$2"
 344:   local log="$3"
 345:   local pid_file="$4"
 346: 
 347:   local deadline=$((SECONDS + STARTUP_TIMEOUT))
 348:   local pid
 349: 
 350:   while [[ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ]]; do
 351:     if curl -sf -o /dev/null "$url"; then
 352:       return 0
 353:     fi
 354: 
 355:     # Stop waiting immediately when the process has already crashed.
 356:     if [[ -f "$pid_file" ]]; then
 357:       pid="$(cat "$pid_file" 2>/dev/null || true)"
 358: 
 359:       if [[ -n "$pid" ]] && ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
 360:         warn "$label process exited before becoming ready."
 361:         warn "Last lines of $log:"
 362: 
 363:         tail -n 40 "$log" >&2 || true
 364:         return 1
 365:       fi
 366:     fi
 367: 
 368:     sleep 1
 369:   done
 370: 
 371:   warn "$label did not answer within ${STARTUP_TIMEOUT}s."
 372:   warn "Last lines of $log:"
 373: 
 374:   tail -n 40 "$log" >&2 || true
 375:   return 1
 376: }

 503: stop_one() {
 504:   local pid_file="$1"
 505:   local label="$2"
 506: 
 507:   local pid
 508:   local pgid
 509: 
 510:   [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || return 0
 511: 
 512:   pid="$(cat "$pid_file" 2>/dev/null || true)"
 513: 
 514:   if [[ -n "$pid" ]] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then

 516:       ps -o pgid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null |
 517:         tr -d ' ' ||

 524:     else
 525:       kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
 526:     fi
 527: 
 528:     info "stopped $label (pid $pid)"

 530: 
 531:   rm -f "$pid_file"

### A4 — Seam + hai lane thi hành + JSONL ABI, AI3 (3–4 ngày)

#### A4.1. Seam ẩn concrete session (điểm 1)

```python
class RoundHostProtocol(Protocol):
    def declare(self, response: AnalysisResponse) -> None: ...
    def call(self, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult: ...

class AnalystRunner(Protocol):
    def run(self, analysis: AnalysisRequest,
            host: RoundHostProtocol) -> AnalysisResponse: ...
```

- In-process adapter: `declare()` forward vào `host.session.declare(...)`,
  `call()` vào host thật. Container proxy: `declare()` phát frame
  `declare_proposals`, `call()` phát `tool_request`. **Hai lane cùng một seam
  thật sự** — runner không biết session tồn tại.
- Gate nhận `HostSource = Callable[[AnalysisRequest], RoundHostProtocol]`.

#### A4.2. Vòng trong runner + luật revise-redeclare (điểm 6)

```
engine → guard → host.declare(batch 1)
→ [tool_request → tool_result]*
→ revise (≤2 vòng): proposal đổi nội dung ⇒ content hash mới ⇒ ID MỚI
    → host.declare(batch mới)   # TRƯỚC mọi tool request tiếp theo
    → [tool_request → tool_result]*
→ final AnalysisResponse
```

- **Proposal đã declare là immutable** — `declare()` refuse
  `hypothesis_redefined` (protocol.py:427). Revised batch declare trước request
  mới. Proposal bị thay giữ trong audit artifact với quan hệ `supersedes`;
  proposal refuted loại khỏi final nhưng **không xóa lịch sử**.

#### A4.3. JSONL ABI — định nghĩa đủ (điểm 3)

- `stdio_protocol.py` + spec doc. **Frame set:** `hello` · `analysis_request` ·
  `declare_proposals` · `declaration_ack` · `model_request` / `model_response` ·
  `tool_request` / `tool_result` · `final_response` · `error` · `done`.
- **Envelope mọi frame:** `protocol_version` (=
  `ANALYST_RUNNER_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, vào bundle identity —
  `runner_protocol_version`, RFC platform) · `analysis_run_id` · `bundle_id` ·
  `sequence` · `message_type` · `correlation_id` · payload theo schema từng
  loại · giới hạn kích thước frame.
- **State machine + từ chối:** frame sai phase ⇒ reject; duplicate/out-of-order
  `sequence` ⇒ reject; stdout chứa dòng không phải JSON ⇒ error + kill; EOF sớm
  ⇒ chấm như analyst raised; response sau timeout ⇒ bỏ, process đã kill.
  `declare_proposals` ⇒ platform validate batch → `host.session.declare(...)` →
  `declaration_ack` → container mới được gửi `tool_request` (thiếu ack mà
  request ⇒ reject sai phase). Mỗi revise round lặp lại declare → ack.

#### A4.4. Model gateway platform-owned + sandbox (điểm 2)

- **Container KHÔNG có API credential, KHÔNG có outbound network.** Model call
  đi qua frame: container phát `model_request` (messages + config đã
  validate) → platform validate bundle/model/config/**budget** → platform gọi
  provider bằng **credential platform**, config lấy từ bundle đã khóa →
  `model_response` về container. Đúng nguyên văn plan nền :253: "platform giữ
  credential, platform gửi request, prompt/config lấy từ bundle đã khóa".
  Submitted code không đọc được secret, không có đường exfiltrate hidden packet.
- **Sandbox container gate:** filesystem read-only, chỉ mount artifact cần
  thiết · CPU/memory/process/time limits · stdout chỉ dành cho protocol, log đi
  stderr (platform lưu stderr riêng, không parse).
- Dev in-process lane vẫn gọi provider trực tiếp (nhanh); official
  calibration + gate bắt buộc lane container + gateway.

#### A4.5. Đọc ToolResult + task platform

- Non-completed ⇒ không đọc verdict; tôn trọng `unsupported_inferences`;
  `refuted` ⇒ rút proposal; `not_checkable` ⇒ InvestigationRecord giữ ở
  `not_checkable`, không checker-based promotion. 12 mã rejection xử lý theo mã.
- **RFC platform (khai rõ):** `gate.py` đổi sang `HostSource` + drive lane
  container; `bundle.py` thêm `runner_protocol_version`.
- Test: declare-trước-admit; revise-redeclare (id mới, supersedes); budget;
  sequence lệch; frame sai phase; non-JSON stdout; EOF sớm; timeout-kill;

### A6 — Dev calibration + fixture source (1.5–2.5 ngày)

- **Fixture root khớp suite:** `fixtures/golden/visible/<case_id>/{packet.json,
  provenance.json}`.
- **`PacketArtifact` + thuật toán validate ở loader platform** (điểm 8 — không
  tin giá trị caller khai):

  ```python
  class PacketArtifact(BaseModel):
      packet: CasePacket
      packet_checksum: str
      fixture_kind: Literal["synthetic_calibration", "recorded"]
      provenance_checksum: str
  ```

  Loader platform: (1) recompute `packet_checksum` từ canonical CasePacket —
  lệch ⇒ reject; (2) load provenance bằng canonical ref (hoặc embed object);
  (3) recompute `provenance_checksum` — lệch ⇒ reject; (4) kiểm provenance trỏ
  đúng packet checksum + `packet_ref`; (5) **`fixture_kind` do loader suy ra từ
  provenance đã validate**, không nhận từ caller; (6) hidden/preregistered gate
  chỉ nhận `recorded`. Test ở platform (RFC), không chỉ analyst-side.
- `harness.py`: `score_case`/`score_suite`, 6 họ, 6 metric
  `CALIBRATION_TARGETS`.
- **Định nghĩa so sánh (ngưỡng đề xuất, An chỉnh khi approve):** thắng floor =
  structural 0 (bắt buộc, không trade-off) ∧ ≥ `reference_analyst` cả 6 metric
  macro ∧ vượt hẳn ≥ 1 trong {precision, recall@3}. Critic bật mặc định =
  precision hoặc abstention +≥0,05 macro ∧ recall@3 không giảm quá 0,05 ∧
  structural 0.
- **Cache dev:** key `runtime_config_checksum` (§A2); nondeterminism run bypass
  cache/namespace mới; cache hit ≠ repetition — harness assert.
- Kết quả A6 không phải điểm nộp.

### A6.5 — Data readiness golden chính thức (platform, ngoài critical path)

3/6 họ stageable; 3 họ `CANNOT_STAGE_YET`. Việc platform: planted runs với
sidecar → packet fixture `recorded` → mở 3 họ còn lại → flip
`OFFICIAL_GOLDEN_READY` → preregister. A6 chuyển sang packet thật khi xong.

### A7 — Freeze bundle + container + official calibration (1.5–2 ngày)

**Thứ tự: code xong → build container → freeze bundle → calibration chính
bundle đó → đổi gì rebuild + calibration lại → nộp.**

- **Freeze đòi clean tree** (`git status --porcelain` rỗng; tree bẩn ⇒ builder
  refuse). `agent_code_digest = git:<SHA>`.
- **Model identity preflight**: gọi provider, `response.model` không rỗng +
  khớp configured, freeze làm `model_revision`.
- `Dockerfile.analyst`: image chạy lane stdio. `container_digest` = digest image.
- `bundle_builder.py`: đủ field gồm `runner_protocol_version` +
  `generation_parameters` flatten (§A2).
- **Official calibration = 3 lượt qua lane container + gateway, luật pass bảo
  thủ** (điểm 7):
  1. cả 3 lượt `structural_violations = 0`;
  2. không lượt nào có protocol/runtime error;
  3. model identity khớp preflight ở cả 3;
  4. từng statistical metric lấy **minimum của 3 lượt** so với
     `CALIBRATION_TARGETS`;
  5. **không retry lượt fail** — retry là "best of N".
  Bypass cache (nondeterminism smoke test — không phải ước lượng variance);
  report gắn `bundle_identity_checksum`.
- **Dry gate**: `run_gate(..., allow_visible_suite=True)` qua lane container.
- Test: tree bẩn refuse; thiếu field refuse; identity ổn định; calibration từ
  chối bundle chưa freeze; identity drift giữa chừng ⇒ hủy; lượt fail không
  retry.

Viết sau khi hidden gate pass. Scope tối thiểu: async route + job states +
idempotency · flag theo `GateDecision` verified · timeout/cost budget +
degrade · artifact retention + transcript · authorization · fallback panel
deterministic E4 · controlled rollout. Plan này dừng ở bundle qua official
calibration + dry gate.

```python

    def declare(self, response: AnalysisResponse) -> None: ...
    def call(self, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult: ...

```

- In-process adapter: `declare()` forward vào `host.session.declare(...)`,

```

→ [tool_request → tool_result]*
→ revise (≤2 vòng): proposal đổi nội dung ⇒ content hash mới ⇒ ID MỚI

tool_response:
---
name: plan
description: Strategic planning with optional interview workflow
---

<Purpose>
Plan creates comprehensive, actionable work plans through intelligent interaction. It auto-detects whether to interview the user (broad requests) or plan directly (detailed requests), and supports consensus mode (iterative Planner/Architect/Critic loop with RALPLAN-DR structured deliberation) and review mode (Critic evaluation of existing plans).
</Purpose>

<Use_When>
- User wants to plan before implementing -- "plan this", "plan the", "let's plan"
- User wants structured requirements gathering for a vague idea
- User wants an existing plan reviewed -- "review this plan", `--review`
- User wants multi-perspective consensus on a plan -- `--consensus`, "ralplan"
- Task is broad or vague and needs scoping before any code is written
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- User wants autonomous end-to-end execution -- use `autopilot` instead
- User wants to start coding immediately with a clear task -- use `ralph` or delegate to executor
- User asks a simple question that can be answered directly -- just answer it
- Task is a single focused fix with obvious scope -- skip planning, just do it
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Why_This_Exists>
Jumping into code without understanding requirements leads to rework, scope creep, and missed edge cases. Plan provides structured requirements gathering, expert analysis, and quality-gated plans so that execution starts from a solid foundation. The consensus mode adds multi-perspective validation for high-stakes projects.
</Why_This_Exists>

<Execution_Policy>
- Auto-detect interview vs direct mode based on request specificity
- Ask one question at a time during interviews -- never batch multiple questions
- Gather codebase facts via `explore` agent before asking the user about them
- When session guidance enables `USE_OMX_EXPLORE_CMD`, prefer `omx explore` for simple read-only repository lookups during planning; keep prompts narrow and concrete, and keep prompt-heavy or ambiguous planning work on the richer normal path and fall back normally if `omx explore` is unavailable.
- Plans must meet quality standards: 80%+ claims cite file/line, 90%+ criteria are testable
- Implementation step count must be right-sized to task scope; avoid defaulting to exactly five steps when the work is clearly smaller or larger
- Consensus mode outputs the final plan by default; add `--interactive` to enable execution handoff
- Consensus mode uses RALPLAN-DR short mode by default; switch to deliberate mode with `--deliberate` or when the request explicitly signals high risk (auth/security, data migration, destructive/irreversible changes, production incident, compliance/PII, public API breakage)
- Default to concise, evidence-dense progress and completion reporting unless the user or risk level requires more detail
- Treat newer user task updates as local overrides for the active workflow branch while preserving earlier non-conflicting constraints
- If correctness depends on additional inspection, retrieval, execution, or verification, keep using the relevant tools until the plan is grounded
- Continue through clear, low-risk, reversible next steps automatically; ask only when the next step is materially branching, destructive, or preference-dependent
</Execution_Policy>

<Steps>

### Mode Selection

| Mode | Trigger | Behavior |
|------|---------|----------|
| Interview | Default for broad requests | Interactive requirements gathering |
| Direct | `--direct`, or detailed request | Skip interview, generate plan directly |
| Consensus | `--consensus`, "ralplan" | Planner -> Architect -> Critic loop until agreement with RALPLAN-DR structured deliberation (short by default, `--deliberate` for high-risk); outputs plan by default |
| Consensus Interactive | `--consensus --interactive` | Same as Consensus but pauses for user feedback at draft and approval steps, then hands off to execution |
| Review | `--review`, "review this plan" | Critic evaluation of existing plan |

### Interview Mode (broad/vague requests)

1. **Classify the request**: Broad (vague verbs, no specific files, touches 3+ areas) triggers interview mode
2. **Ask one focused question** using `AskUserQuestion` for preferences, scope, and constraints
3. **Gather codebase facts first**: Before asking "what patterns does your code use?", spawn an `explore` agent to find out, then ask informed follow-up questions
4. **Build on answers**: Each question builds on the previous answer
5. **Consult Analyst** (THOROUGH tier) for hidden requirements, edge cases, and risks
6. **Create plan** when the user signals readiness: "create the plan", "I'm ready", "make it a work plan"

### Direct Mode (detailed requests)

1. **Quick Analysis**: Optional brief Analyst consultation
2. **Create plan**: Generate comprehensive work plan immediately
3. **Review** (optional): Critic review if requested

### Consensus Mode (`--consensus` / "ralplan")

**RALPLAN-DR modes**: **Short** (default, bounded structure) and **Deliberate** (for `--deliberate` or explicit high-risk requests). Both modes keep the same Planner -> Architect -> Critic sequence. The workflow auto-proceeds through planning steps (Planner/Architect/Critic) but outputs the final plan without executing.

1. **Planner** creates initial plan and a compact **RALPLAN-DR summary** before any Architect review. The summary **MUST** include:
   - **Principles** (3-5)
   - **Decision Drivers** (top 3)
   - **Viable Options** (>=2) with bounded pros/cons for each option
   - If only one viable option remains, an explicit **invalidation rationale** for the alternatives that were rejected
   - In **deliberate mode**: a **pre-mortem** (3 failure scenarios) and an **expanded test plan** covering **unit / integration / e2e / observability**
2. **User feedback** *(--interactive only)*: If running with `--interactive`, **MUST** use `AskUserQuestion` to present the draft plan **plus the RALPLAN-DR Principles / Decision Drivers / Options summary for early direction alignment** with these options:
   - **Proceed to review** â€” send to Architect and Critic for evaluation
   - **Request changes** â€” return to step 1 with user feedback incorporated
   - **Skip review** â€” go directly to final approval (step 7)
   If NOT running with `--interactive`, automatically proceed to review (step 3).
3. **Architect** reviews for architectural soundness using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "architect"`. Architect review **MUST** include: strongest steelman counterargument (antithesis) against the favored option, at least one meaningful tradeoff tension, and (when possible) a synthesis path. In deliberate mode, Architect should explicitly flag principle violations. **Wait for this step to complete before proceeding to step 4.** Do NOT run steps 3 and 4 in parallel.
4. **Critic** evaluates against quality criteria using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "critic"`. Critic **MUST** verify principle-option consistency, fair alternative exploration, risk mitigation clarity, testable acceptance criteria, and concrete verification steps. Critic **MUST** explicitly reject shallow alternatives, driver contradictions, vague risks, or weak verification. In deliberate mode, Critic **MUST** reject missing/weak pre-mortem or missing/weak expanded test plan. Run only after step 3 is complete.
5. **Re-review loop** (max 5 iterations): If Critic rejects or iterates, execute this closed loop:
   a. Collect all feedback from Architect + Critic
   b. Pass feedback to Planner to produce a revised plan
   c. **Return to Step 3** â€” Architect reviews the revised plan
   d. **Return to Step 4** â€” Critic evaluates the revised plan
   e. Repeat until Critic approves OR max 5 iterations reached
   f. If max iterations reached without approval, present the best version to user via `AskUserQuestion` with note that expert consensus was not reached
6. **Apply improvements**: When reviewers approve with improvement suggestions, merge all accepted improvements into the plan file before proceeding. Final consensus output **MUST** include an **ADR** section with: **Decision**, **Drivers**, **Alternatives considered**, **Why chosen**, **Consequences**, **Follow-ups**. Specifically:
   a. Collect all improvement suggestions from Architect and Critic responses
   b. Deduplicate and categorize the suggestions
   c. Update the plan file in `.omx/plans/` with the accepted improvements (add missing details, refine steps, strengthen acceptance criteria, ADR updates, etc.)
   d. Note which improvements were applied in a brief changelog section at the end of the plan
   e. Before any execution handoff, derive an explicit **available-agent-types roster** from the known prompt catalog and add concrete **follow-up staffing guidance** for both `$ralph` and `$team` (recommended roles, counts, suggested reasoning levels by lane, and why each lane exists)
   f. For the `$team` path, add an explicit launch-hint block with concrete `omx team` / `$team` commands and a **team verification path** (what team proves before shutdown, what Ralph verifies after handoff)
7. On Critic approval (with improvements applied): *(--interactive only)* If running with `--interactive`, use `AskUserQuestion` to present the plan with these options:
   - **Approve and execute** â€” proceed to implementation via ralph+ultrawork
   - **Approve and implement via team** â€” proceed to implementation via coordinated parallel team agents
   - **Request changes** â€” return to step 1 with user feedback
   - **Reject** â€” discard the plan entirely
   If NOT running with `--interactive`, output the final approved plan and stop. Do NOT auto-execute.
8. *(--interactive only)* User chooses via the structured `AskUserQuestion` UI (never ask for approval in plain text)
9. On user approval (--interactive only):
   - **Approve and execute**: **MUST** invoke `$ralph` with the approved plan path from `.omx/plans/` as context **plus the explicit available-agent-types roster, suggested reasoning levels, concrete role allocation guidance, and direct launch hints for Ralph follow-up work**. Do NOT implement directly. Do NOT edit source code files in the planning agent. The ralph skill handles execution via ultrawork parallel agents.
   - **Approve and implement via team**: **MUST** invoke `$team` with the approved plan path from `.omx/plans/` as context **plus the explicit available-agent-types roster, suggested reasoning levels, concrete staffing / worker-role allocation guidance, explicit `omx team` / `$team` launch hints, and the team verification path**. Do NOT implement directly. The team skill coordinates parallel agents across the staged pipeline for faster execution on large tasks.

### Review Mode (`--review`)

0. Treat review as a reviewer-only pass. The context that wrote the plan, cleanup proposal, or diff MUST NOT be the context that approves it.
1. Read plan file from `.omx/plans/`
2. Evaluate via Critic using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "critic"`
3. For cleanup/refactor/anti-slop work, verify that the artifact includes a cleanup plan, regression tests or an explicit test gap, smell-by-smell passes, and quality gates.
4. Return verdict: APPROVED, REVISE (with specific feedback), or REJECT (replanning required)
5. If the current context authored the artifact, hand the review to `/review`, `critic`, `quality-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, or `verifier` as appropriate.

### Plan Output Format

Every plan includes:
- Requirements Summary
- Acceptance Criteria (testable)
- Implementation Steps (with file references)
- Adaptive step count sized to the actual scope (not a fixed five-step template)
- Risks and Mitigations
- Verification Steps
- For consensus/ralplan: **RALPLAN-DR summary** (Principles, Decision Drivers, Options)
- For consensus/ralplan final output: **ADR** (Decision, Drivers, Alternatives considered, Why chosen, Consequences, Follow-ups)
- For consensus/ralplan execution handoff: **Available-Agent-Types Roster**, **Follow-up Staffing Guidance** (including suggested reasoning levels by lane), explicit `omx team` / `$team` **Launch Hints**, and **Team Verification Path**
- For deliberate consensus mode: **Pre-mortem (3 scenarios)** and **Expanded Test Plan** (unit/integration/e2e/observability)

Plans are saved to `.omx/plans/`. Drafts go to `.omx/drafts/`.
</Steps>

<Tool_Usage>
- Before first MCP tool use, call `ToolSearch("mcp")` to discover deferred MCP tools
- Use `AskUserQuestion` for preference questions (scope, priority, timeline, risk tolerance) -- provides clickable UI
- Use plain text for questions needing specific values (port numbers, names, follow-up clarifications)
- Use the `explore` agent (LOW tier, bounded quick pass) to gather codebase facts before asking the user
- Use `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "planner"` for planning validation on large-scope plans
- Use `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "analyst"` for requirements analysis
- Use `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "critic"` for plan review in consensus and review modes
- If ToolSearch finds no MCP tools or Codex is unavailable, fall back to equivalent OMX prompt agents -- never block on external tools
- **CRITICAL â€” Consensus mode agent calls MUST be sequential, never parallel.** Always await the Architect result before issuing the Critic call.
- In consensus mode, default to RALPLAN-DR short mode; enable deliberate mode on `--deliberate` or explicit high-risk signals (auth/security, migrations, destructive changes, production incidents, compliance/PII, public API breakage)
- In consensus mode with `--interactive`: use `AskUserQuestion` for the user feedback step (step 2) and the final approval step (step 7) -- never ask for approval in plain text. Without `--interactive`, auto-proceed through planning steps without pausing. Output the final plan without execution.
- In consensus mode with `--interactive`, on user approval **MUST** invoke `$ralph` for execution (step 9) -- never implement directly in the planning agent
- In consensus mode, execution follow-up handoff **MUST** include an explicit available-agent-types roster plus concrete staffing / role-allocation guidance grounded in that roster, suggested reasoning levels by lane, explicit `omx team` / `$team` launch hints, and a team verification path
</Tool_Usage>


## Scenario Examples

**Good:** The user says `continue` after the workflow already has a clear next step. Continue the current branch of work instead of restarting or re-asking the same question.

**Good:** The user changes only the output shape or downstream delivery step (for example `make a PR`). Preserve earlier non-conflicting workflow constraints and apply the update locally.

**Bad:** The user says `continue`, and the workflow restarts discovery or stops before the missing verification/evidence is gathered.

<Examples>
<Good>
Adaptive interview (gathering facts before asking):
```
Planner: [spawns explore agent: "find authentication implementation"]
Planner: [receives: "Auth is in src/auth/ using JWT with passport.js"]
Planner: "I see you're using JWT authentication with passport.js in src/auth/.
         For this new feature, should we extend the existing auth or add a separate auth flow?"
```
Why good: Answers its own codebase question first, then asks an informed preference question.
</Good>

<Good>
Single question at a time:
```
Q1: "What's the main goal?"
A1: "Improve performance"
Q2: "For performance, what matters more -- latency or throughput?"
A2: "Latency"
Q3: "For latency, are we optimizing for p50 or p99?"
```
Why good: Each question builds on the previous answer. Focused and progressive.
</Good>

<Bad>
Asking about things you could look up:
```
Planner: "Where is authentication implemented in your codebase?"
User: "Uh, somewhere in src/auth I think?"
```
Why bad: The planner should spawn an explore agent to find this, not ask the user.
</Bad>

<Bad>
Batching multiple questions:
```
"What's the scope? And the timeline? And who's the audience?"
```
Why bad: Three questions at once causes shallow answers. Ask one at a time.
</Bad>

<Bad>
Presenting all design options at once:
```
"Here are 4 approaches: Option A... Option B... Option C... Option D... Which do you prefer?"
```
Why bad: Decision fatigue. Present one option with trade-offs, get reaction, then present the next.
</Bad>
</Examples>

<Escalation_And_Stop_Conditions>
- Stop interviewing when requirements are clear enough to plan -- do not over-interview
- In consensus mode, stop after 5 Planner/Architect/Critic iterations and present the best version
- Consensus mode outputs the plan by default; with `--interactive`, user can approve and hand off to ralph/team
- If the user says "just do it" or "skip planning", **MUST** invoke `$ralph` to transition to execution mode. Do NOT implement directly in the planning agent.
- Escalate to the user when there are irreconcilable trade-offs that require a business decision
</Escalation_And_Stop_Conditions>

<Final_Checklist>
- [ ] Plan has testable acceptance criteria (90%+ concrete)
- [ ] Plan references specific files/lines where applicable (80%+ claims)
- [ ] All risks have mitigations identified
- [ ] No vague terms without metrics ("fast" -> "p99 < 200ms")
- [ ] Plan saved to `.omx/plans/`
- [ ] In consensus mode: RALPLAN-DR summary includes 3-5 principles, top 3 drivers, and >=2 viable options (or explicit invalidation rationale)
- [ ] In consensus mode final output: ADR section included (Decision / Drivers / Alternatives considered / Why chosen / Consequences / Follow-ups)
- [ ] In deliberate consensus mode: pre-mortem (3 scenarios) + expanded test plan (unit/integration/e2e/observability) included
- [ ] In consensus mode with `--interactive`: user explicitly approved before any execution; without `--interactive`: output final plan after Critic approval (no auto-execution)
</Final_Checklist>

<Advanced>
## Design Option Presentation

When presenting design choices during interviews, chunk them:

1. **Overview** (2-3 sentences)
2. **Option A** with trade-offs
3. [Wait for user reaction]
4. **Option B** with trade-offs
5. [Wait for user reaction]
6. **Recommendation** (only after options discussed)

Format for each option:
```
### Option A: [Name]
**Approach:** [1 sentence]
**Pros:** [bullets]
**Cons:** [bullets]

What's your reaction to this approach?
```

## Question Classification

Before asking any interview question, classify it:

| Type | Examples | Action |
|------|----------|--------|
| Codebase Fact | "What patterns exist?", "Where is X?" | Explore first, do not ask user |
| User Preference | "Priority?", "Timeline?" | Ask user via AskUserQuestion |
| Scope Decision | "Include feature Y?" | Ask user |
| Requirement | "Performance constraints?" | Ask user |

## Review Quality Criteria

| Criterion | Standard |
|-----------|----------|
| Clarity | 80%+ claims cite file/line |
| Testability | 90%+ criteria are concrete |
| Verification | All file refs exist |
| Specificity | No vague terms |

## Deprecation Notice

The separate `/planner`, `/ralplan`, and `/review` skills have been merged into `$plan`. All workflows (interview, direct, consensus, review) are available through `$plan`.
</Advanced>

  84: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  85: class ProviderTurn:
  86:     """A provider's own serialisation of an assistant turn, kept intact.
  87: 
  88:     ``text`` and ``tool_calls`` are the parts the agent understands, and
  89:     for a long time they were all this layer kept. That loses whatever
  90:     else the vendor attached — and some vendors *require* it back on the
  91:     next request:
  92: 
  93:     * Gemini signs each function call with a ``thought_signature`` and
  94:       rejects the follow-up turn without it ("Function call is missing a
  95:       thought_signature");
  96:     * Anthropic requires thinking blocks echoed back unchanged while a
  97:       turn is still in progress.
  98: 
  99:     Rebuilding the assistant message from the parsed fields drops both.
 100:     So the provider stores its raw payload here and replays it verbatim
 101:     instead of reconstructing it.
 102: 
 103:     ``format`` names the wire format, not the vendor: every
 104:     OpenAI-compatible provider shares one. A provider must ignore a turn
 105:     whose format it does not recognise — that is what makes a transcript
 106:     safe to carry across a provider switch.
 107:     """
 108: 
 109:     format: str
 110:     payload: Mapping[str, Any]
 111: 
 112: 
 113: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 114: class LLMMessage:
 115:     """One conversation turn.
 116: 
 117:     A user turn carries either free text or tool results; an assistant
 118:     turn carries text and/or tool calls. Keeping both on one type means
 119:     the transcript is a plain list, which is trivial to persist.
 120:     """
 121: 
 122:     role: MessageRole
 123:     text: str = ""
 124:     tool_calls: tuple[ToolCall, ...] = ()
 125:     tool_results: tuple[ToolResult, ...] = ()
 126:     #: Set on assistant turns that came back from a provider. Replayed
 127:     #: verbatim so vendor metadata survives the round trip.
 128:     provider_turn: ProviderTurn | None = None
 129: 
 130:     @staticmethod
 131:     def user(text: str) -> LLMMessage:
 132:         return LLMMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, text=text)
 133: 
 134:     @staticmethod
 135:     def assistant(
 136:         text: str = "",
 137:         tool_calls: Sequence[ToolCall] = (),
 138:         provider_turn: ProviderTurn | None = None,
 139:     ) -> LLMMessage:
 140:         return LLMMessage(
 141:             role=MessageRole.ASSISTANT,
 142:             text=text,
 143:             tool_calls=tuple(tool_calls),
 144:             provider_turn=provider_turn,
 145:         )
